identity.title: Tight Lower Bounds under Asymmetric High-Order Hölder Smoothness and Uniform Convexity

problem.claim: Characterize oracle complexity for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth, uniformly convex functions under asymmetric relationships between smoothness and convexity orders.

contributions.claim: Derives worst-case oracle-complexity lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes q > p+ν and q < p+ν, under access to derivatives through order p.
Uses an ℓ∞-ball-truncated-Gaussian smoothed hard function in the first asymmetric regime.
Extends prior lower bounds for first- and second-order smoothness and for uniformly convex functions, with reported agreement with corresponding upper bounds.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their results generalize several prior lower-bound settings and match upper bounds in the general high-order asymmetric setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an Ω((H/σ)^{2/(3(p+ν)-2)}(σ/ε)^{2(q-p-ν)/(q(3(p+ν)-2))}) lower bound for q > p+ν, for reaching an ε-approximate solution measured by optimality gap.
The authors report an Ω((H/σ)^{2/(3(p+ν)-2)} + log log((σ^{p+ν}/H^q)^{1/(p+ν-q)}(1/ε))) lower bound for q < p+ν.
The authors report that these lower bounds match corresponding upper bounds in the stated general setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies oracle complexity for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth and uniformly convex functions.
It separates the analysis into the asymmetric cases q > p+ν and q < p+ν.
For pth-order oracle access, it gives regime-specific worst-case lower bounds for ε-approximate solutions measured by optimality gap.
It presents the analysis as a generalization of earlier smoothness and uniform-convexity lower bounds and reports matching upper bounds.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly partitions the result by the ordering of q and p+ν and states separate complexity expressions for each regime.

lessons.interpretation: When parameter relationships change the form of the guarantee, regime-specific claims can make the theorem's scope and dependence easier to interpret.
lessons.application: State the governing parameter regimes before presenting bounds, then attach each expression to its exact regime and approximation criterion.
lessons.exception: This structure is less useful when the parameter dependence is genuinely uniform or when additional regimes would make the presentation disproportionate.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide proof details, dimensional assumptions, oracle-model conventions beyond access through order p, or constants and validity conditions for the displayed bounds.
The reported match to upper bounds is not detailed enough here to identify the compared algorithms, parameter ranges, or whether the comparison is exact in all dependencies.
